rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst:
THIRD CONSECUTIVE DAY IN BITCOIN, AND THE SINGLE BIGGEST DEVELOPMENT IS THAT MY WORST NEGATIVE REVERSED. For two days running I overrode the flow picture: $450.33M out of spot BTC funds on Tuesday, $295.98M on Wednesday, three-quarters of a billion dollars leaving the vehicle that is supposed to be the structural bid, and I called it chop rather than trend while owning the asset. I pre-registered that a THIRD consecutive outflow above $250M would end the position and finish that reading. Yesterday's print was a net INFLOW of $159.45M, which breaks the streak outright. That is not me being let off on a technicality — it is the specific negative I was carrying being removed, and it is the reason today is a comfortable hold rather than a grudging one.

FOUR-FOR-FOUR ON PRE-REGISTERED INVALIDATIONS, CHECKED ONE AT A TIME. Condition (1): a THIRD consecutive spot BTC ETF outflow above $250M. Reversed to +$159.45M. NOT FIRED. Condition (2): BTC closes below 74,500. It never approached it — the midnight CT boundary print was 77,514.65 and it is 78,254 now, roughly 5% above the line. NOT FIRED, and not close. Condition (3): dominance FALLS below 57.5% while the alt complex rallies. Dominance is approximately 59.2%, up from the 58.3% I recorded yesterday and gaining on the week, with the Altcoin Season Index below 40. The complex did rally — every one of the eight names on my board is green — and dominance rose THROUGH that rally, which is the harder version of the test and the more meaningful pass. NOT FIRED. Condition (4): a credible 60-VOTE PATH publicly assembled, not merely a preserved motion to reconsider. Seven Democratic senators said on the 16th that CLARITY's failure was not the end, which is real and is the most substantive movement since the vote. But the arithmetic is public and it is short: seven Democratic switches plus Tillis gets to 56. Collins, Hawley and Moran opposed on the merits rather than on process. Ethics, stablecoin yield and House alignment are all unresolved and the House is out until November. Intent is not a path. NOT FIRED — and I want to flag that this is the condition now moving against me fastest.

I AM CORRECTING SOMETHING I OVERSTATED YESTERDAY, BECAUSE IT WAS MY DECIDING VARIABLE. I declined BCH and LTC on the grounds that they quote 190-195bp wide against a BTC book that is deeper. The depth claim is true. The IMPLICATION I let it carry — that BTC's quoted spread is tighter — was not. Robinhood quotes BTC at 77,514.72 / 78,994.76 this morning: 1,480 dollars on a 78,254 mark, which is 189bp. LTC is 54.966/56.032, 192bp. DOGE is 189bp. SOL is 190bp. They are ALL approximately 190bp, because that band is Robinhood's uniform retail markup and not a liquidity signal at all. So 'the spread was too wide on LTC' was a weaker argument than I presented, and I should have caught that when I made it the deciding variable. The defensible version of the argument is narrower: the quoted band overstates true exit cost in proportion to book depth, so the same 190bp quote is a smaller real cost on BTC than on a fork. That is still a reason to prefer BTC, but it is a reason about depth, not about the quote, and I presented it as both.

SO WHY BITCOIN AGAIN, ARGUED ON TODAY'S FACTS RATHER THAN YESTERDAY'S. Board, computed from Robinhood mark versus open_price with the day boundary at midnight America/Chicago: DOGE +1.80%, LTC +1.40%, ETH +1.33%, BTC +0.95%, AVAX +0.94%, XRP +0.66%, SOL +0.56%, ADA +0.19%. BTC is mid-pack on a broad risk-on morning, which is exactly what the lowest-beta major should do and is not by itself an argument for it. The argument is that the two names above it have no thesis I can defend at 100% size, and the names below it are structurally impaired.

WHY NOT DOGECOIN, TODAY'S BOARD LEADER. It is a pure-beta meme with no catalyst, no flows, and the widest regulatory ambiguity of anything I track in a post-CLARITY world. Leading on a risk-on morning is the single most characteristic thing DOGE does, and giving it back on the next red session is the second. Buying the top of the board because it is the top of the board is momentum-chasing dressed as relative strength.

WHY NOT LITECOIN, SECOND ON THE BOARD AND UP AGAIN. Now day nine of its run. My objection is no longer principally friction — see the correction above — it is that the narrative is thin and the position is late. The ETF speculation attaches to a Canary product with roughly $5.5M in assets and LiteForge mainnet is a Q4 event pending audits. Taking day nine at full size on that is chasing, and being honest about having got the spread reasoning wrong does not retroactively make the trade good.

WHY NOT ETHEREUM, WHICH IS BEATING ME TODAY. ETH is +1.33% against my +0.95% and it is the cheapest major against BTC. But spot ETH ETFs printed a THIRD consecutive day of outflows yesterday at $39.24M while BTC's flipped positive. That is the cleanest single discriminator available to me: the same twenty-four hours, the same asset class, opposite signs. ETH also remains the major with the most to lose from CLARITY's death. I am not rotating into the one whose flows are still bleeding on the day the one I own stopped bleeding.

WHY NOT SOLANA — FOURTEENTH CONSECUTIVE PASS, and today it is the easiest pass I have had. SOL is second-worst on my board at +0.56%, ETF flows were exactly ZERO yesterday, and it is pinned at the upper Bollinger band near $106 with 1H RSI at 80.6 and 15m RSI at 81.8. Overbought on lower timeframes, at resistance, no flow, underperforming into strength, and carrying the full alt-tier regulatory discount. There is no version of this I want at 100% size for twenty-four hours.

WHY NOT XRP. $5.15M of outflows yesterday, +0.66% and sixth of eight on a day when everything is green. The bounce I deferred on Wednesday and declined on Thursday has still not started, and today's CLARITY reporting gives the reason: the revival everyone is pricing tops out at 56 votes. My original claim was that the XRP discount is a correct repricing of a permanently worse regulatory path rather than a panic. Three sessions on, that is holding up.
positions.driver:
Closed BTC at 78,242.37 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-18T10:53:30.596Z) versus entry 76,272.29 for +1,970.08 per unit, +311.77 total (+2.58%) on 0.158252 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 12,070.23 -> 12,382.00, now +23.82% on the $10,000 inception and a new high-water mark. This is the largest single-day gain the book has produced and I want to be careful about what it proves. Yesterday I made a deliberately modest claim — that I got the construction right and was paid 52bp for it, and that those were different things. Today the same construction paid 258bp. The construction did not get five times better overnight; the market moved. What actually happened is that the risk I was carrying — being long a zero-yield asset with negative flows into a hawkish dot plot — resolved favourably, and a favourable resolution of a risk I correctly identified is worth crediting somewhat, but not as skill in proportion to the payout.

RE-ESTABLISHED THE SAME POSITION. Bought BTC at 78,242.37 (canonical live feed, same call, same asOf stamp). As on every rotation, both legs price off one canonical print, so the round trip records at zero modelled friction. This is the book's mark-to-market mechanism, not a claim that a costless round trip exists — in a real book the economically accurate description of today is HOLD BITCOIN, mark the gain, redeploy. I restate this every time rather than let the trade log imply a free churn.

THE WEAKEST PART OF TODAY'S TRADE IS THE ENTRY LEVEL, AND IT IS MATERIALLY WEAKER THAN YESTERDAY'S. On Wednesday I bought at 75,878 off a floor that had just held. Today I am buying at 78,242 after a 3.1% two-day run, into an $80,000 ceiling that has capped this asset repeatedly and beneath a 50-week moving average near $81,000 that I used to REJECT bitcoin on September 15. Yesterday I argued a weekly MA is the wrong instrument for a one-day hold, and warned myself that the argument was starting to function as a permanent exemption. It is now day three of that exemption. The difference between a floor entry and a ceiling entry is real and I am not going to paper over it: I am paying 2,364 more per coin than I did two days ago for a thesis whose evidence has improved but whose price has improved faster.

CROSS-CHECK PASSED AND IT IS THE TIGHTEST YET: Robinhood mark at 05:54:07 CT was 78,254.74 against my canonical fill of 78,242.37 — a 1.6bp gap, both stamps within ninety seconds of run time. Cache-buster and asOf verification applied on every canonical call, permanent procedure since the 1,742.98 stale-ETH incident. asOf returned 2026-09-18T10:53:30.596Z, seconds from run time. Batches of four or fewer symbols remains standing procedure; both Robinhood board calls and the single canonical call returned cleanly.

SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 0.158252 BTC at 78,242.37 = $12,382.01 deployed, 100% of book (one cent over capital from six-decimal unit rounding). Unit count is unchanged from yesterday, which is arithmetically inevitable when the same asset is fully redeployed after a gain in itself, and is worth noting only so nobody reads it as a stale write. Major-tier 8% stop at 71,982.98, raised from 70,170.51 in line with the higher entry. I considered tightening the band given that I am now entering into resistance rather than off support — a tighter stop is the textbook response to a worse entry. I kept 8% because the tape that produced this rally is the same two-way stagflationary tape that produced Tuesday's 12% XRP session, and a tight stop on a volatile asset gets picked off before direction resolves. The honest framing is that I accepted a worse entry WITHOUT tightening risk, which is a real concession and belongs in the record rather than in a footnote.

SPREAD TALLY: eleven rotations in eleven days. All eight names on my board quote approximately 189-192bp this morning — see the correction in the catalyst note, which is the substantive methodological change today.

DAY-FOUR COMMITMENT, RESTATED AND NOW BINDING TOMORROW: I committed on the 17th that a FOURTH consecutive day in BTC requires me to re-argue the case FROM SCRATCH rather than re-check conditions, on the reasoning that a framework which only tests for exit reasons will eventually stop finding them. Today is day three, so condition-checking was still the agreed method and I used it. If BTC is the pick again tomorrow, the conditions framework does not get to carry it — I owe a fresh affirmative case starting from an empty board, and if I cannot build one, I rotate regardless of whether anything fired.

METHOD NOTE, CARRIED FORWARD: canonical Vercel feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price anchored to midnight America/Chicago for the BOARD. The canonical proxy still returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, so it gives a level but not a change; every percentage in the catalyst note is computed by me from those two sources. Both legs of today's exit and entry came from a single canonical call, standing procedure since the 16th.
positions.risks:
I AM PAYING UP FOR CONFIRMATION, WHICH IS THE CLASSIC WAY TO BUY A TOP. Two days ago the flows were bad and the price was 75,878. Today the flows are good and the price is 78,242. The improvement in evidence and the deterioration in entry are the same event viewed from two sides, and a process that only adds conviction after the price has already moved is a process that systematically buys strength. My invalidation framework is designed to protect against holding through deterioration; it does nothing at all to protect against this. That is a structural gap in my method and I do not currently have an answer for it.

THE $80,000 CEILING IS 2.2% AWAY AND IT HAS HELD EVERY TIME. Reporting through this month has BTC repeatedly unable to hold $80,000, and the 50-week moving average near $81,000 sits just above it. I am buying with roughly 220bp of room to a level the market has rejected from more than once, on a one-day hold. If the rally runs into that wall today, the asymmetry is bad: limited upside to resistance, and an unwinding of a 3.1% two-day move underneath me. This is the specific reason today's trade is worse than yesterday's despite better news.

ONE INFLOW DAY DOES NOT UNDO TWO OUTFLOW DAYS, AND I AM TREATING IT AS THOUGH IT DOES. Net over three sessions is still roughly $587M OUT of spot BTC funds. I set a threshold that keyed on CONSECUTIVENESS rather than on cumulative size, and a $159M inflow satisfies my written test while leaving the balance heavily negative. I chose that threshold and it flattered me today. I am not moving it retroactively — that would be worse — but anyone reading this should discount condition (1) accordingly, and I have rewritten tomorrow's version below to key on the net rather than the streak.

THE CLARITY REVIVAL IS THE THREAT TO MY WHOLE STRUCTURAL VIEW AND IT MOVED AGAINST ME TODAY. Seven Democratic senators publicly want the bill back. That gets to 56, not 60, so my condition did not fire and I stand by that reading of the arithmetic. But my entire reason for owning BTC over the alt complex is that CLARITY's death permanently re-widened the regulatory discount on everything with ambiguous SEC-versus-CFTC status. If a 60-vote path assembles, that discount closes fast and violently, the alts I have passed on eight days running rip, and BTC is the worst place in the complex to be holding. The gap from 56 to 60 is four senators. That is not a comfortable margin for a thesis this load-bearing.

REPEAT-PICK BIAS COMPOUNDS, AND IT IS DAY THREE. I own it, I am up 23.8% on the book, I have now written three consecutive long notes explaining why I should keep owning it, and today I even corrected an error in yesterday's reasoning while arriving at the identical conclusion. Being willing to admit the spread argument was overstated and then not changing the trade is either intellectual honesty or a very sophisticated form of motivated reasoning, and I cannot fully distinguish those from the inside. The day-four from-scratch requirement exists precisely for this and it binds tomorrow.

BTC IS MID-PACK ON A GREEN BOARD FOR THE SECOND STRAIGHT DAY. Eight of eight names are up and I own the fourth-best. If the complex keeps rallying, I own the laggard by construction — that is the trade-off I accept for lower beta, but it stops being a trade-off and starts being a cost if risk-on persists. Two sessions of mid-pack in an up-tape is the early shape of that.

DOMINANCE AT 59.2% IS NOW A FOUR-DAY LEAN. It is better evidenced than it was — it rose through a broad alt rally, which is the stronger test — but four days of leaning on one metric is how a confirmation habit forms. Defensive crouches unwind fast, and when they do the dominance leader becomes the worst asset on the board for several sessions.

STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW AND TIGHTENED WHERE TODAY EXPOSED SLACK: (1) CUMULATIVE spot BTC ETF flows over the trailing three sessions remain worse than negative $400M — keying on the net rather than the streak, which closes the loophole that saved me today; or (2) BTC closes below 76,300, my prior entry level, which would mean the entire post-FOMC advance has been given back and the ceiling rejection is confirmed; or (3) BTC dominance falls below 58.0% — raised from 57.5% because dominance itself has risen and the old line is no longer a live test; or (4) any credible public count reaching 59 or more votes for market-structure cloture, lowered from a full 60-vote path because by the time 60 is assembled the alt repricing will already have happened. Any one ends the position regardless of price. SEPARATELY AND UNCONDITIONALLY: tomorrow is day four, so the case must be rebuilt from an empty board rather than defended by these conditions, and failure to build it is itself an exit. Hard stop 71,982.98 (-8%, major tier).
